case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns Bluetooth qualification planning for an audio module based on a QCC3095-class chipset that is intended to be registered under the customer's company name. The consultant reviews the proposed qualification approach and requests clarification on the qualification status of the module, host stack, and supported profiles before preparing a final quotation. The discussion focuses on determining which existing qualifications can be reused and which test evidence would still be required. After learning that the module is not already qualified, the consultant provides a qualification path and associated test scope assumptions for an HCI-style module implementation.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main technical issue is whether the module itself is already Bluetooth qualified and whether an existing module QDID or Declaration Number can be reused. The consultant explains that including only a qualified SoC is insufficient to avoid RF and RF PHY testing at the module level unless a qualified module design is also available. The thread also examines whether the host stack and audio profiles are already covered by existing qualifications or whether they would require additional protocol qualification work. A distinction is made between a Core-Controller (HCI-style) module qualification path and a more complex qualification path involving unqualified host software or profiles.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant determines the qualification path by identifying the highest-level reusable qualified design available. If only a qualified SoC is available, module-level RF and RF PHY evidence is still required. If the module functions as a typical HCI/Core-Controller implementation and an appropriate controller qualification can be included, qualification can proceed with RF and RF PHY testing plus registration activities. However, if the host stack or profiles are not already qualified, significant additional protocol qualification obligations may apply.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming that a qualified chipset automatically qualifies the module could result in missing RF or RF PHY qualification evidence and an invalid registration strategy. Failing to verify the qualification status of the host stack or supported profiles could unexpectedly introduce major protocol-testing requirements, resulting in substantial additional effort, cost, and schedule impact. Selecting the wrong qualification architecture before quotation could lead to inaccurate project estimates and rework.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For Bluetooth module qualifications, always verify qualification status separately for the SoC, module, controller, host stack, and profiles before defining the qualification path. Reuse eligibility must be evaluated at the correct design level because qualification obligations can change dramatically depending on which layer is already qualified.
